items.title: What must a quantity tell us?
items.student: Classify these fictional reports as scalar or vector quantities and explain:mass10kg,time2s,distance12m,speed4m/s,temperature25°C,displacement3m east,velocity4m/s north,force6N west. Draw arrows for displacements4m east and4m west using1cm for1m. Are equal magnitudes sufficient for equivalent vectors? A walker travels3m east then3m west;compare total distance with displacement. All journeys are paper scenarios,not road activities.
items.teacher: Mass,time,distance,speed,temperature are scalars;displacement,velocity,force require direction as well as magnitude. Opposite4m displacements have equal length but different directions,so are not equivalent. Round trip distance6m,displacement zero. Zero vector has magnitude0 and no unique direction. Illustrations of arrow length/direction support classification;an everyday arrow symbol is not automatically a measured vector.

items.title: Point,arrow and column notation
items.student: Notation:[p;q] denotes the column vector with horizontal component p above vertical component q;points use(x,y). Use one grid unit per coordinate unit. Plot A(−2,1),B(3,4),D(1,−1),E(6,2). Draw directed AB,BA and DE. Write AB using an arrow over AB,a chosen bold vector letter and column notation. Find each column from endpoint minus startpoint. Explain why the point B(3,4) is not the vector AB. If no squared paper is available,copy the supplied grid.
items.teacher: AB=[5;3],BA=[−5;−3],DE=[5;3]. Arrow AB and a consistently defined bold b name the same directed displacement. B's coordinates describe its location relative to the chosen origin;AB's components describe change from A. Use a vertical two-entry column on the board and distinguish it from a coordinate point. Prepare ruler,pencil and reusable squared paper;the supplied blank grid has equal axis scales.

items.title: Equivalent vectors in different places
items.student: On squared paper plot A(0,0),B(4,2),C(−3,−2),D(1,0),E(0,4),F(4,2). Draw AB,CD and EF with arrowheads. Identify equivalent vectors by comparing component changes,length and direction. Compare BA with AB. Explain what changes when a vector is moved parallel to itself without changing its length/direction.
items.teacher: AB=CD=[4;2];EF=[4;−2]. All three have length sqrt20 but EF points differently. BA=[−4;−2] reverses AB. Equivalent free vectors can have different startpoints;position vectors refer to a specified origin. Do not infer equivalence from arrow lengths alone. Verify pupil drawings against endpoint differences and equal grid scales.

items.title: Head-to-tail addition
items.student: Draw a=[3;1] from O(0,0). From its head draw a copy of b=[−1;2]. Draw the resultant from O to the final head and give its components. Repeat b then a. Draw a parallelogram check. Explain why adding arrow lengths alone need not give resultant magnitude. Use equal grid scales and label arrow directions.
items.teacher: O→(3,1)→(2,3);resultant a+b=[2;3]. Reverse order O→(−1,2)→(2,3) reaches the same point. Parallelogram opposite sides are copies of a and b and the diagonal from the shared tail is the resultant. Magnitude sqrt13,whereas individual magnitudes sqrt10 and sqrt5 do not add to it. Numeric magnitude is a teacher extension until Lesson8;the directional diagram already disproves adding lengths.

items.title: Component addition and a route check
items.student: A paper route has successive displacements u=[4;−3],v=[−2;5],w=[−1;−2],in metres. Find u+v and u+v+w by components and by a head-to-tail sketch. Compare(u+v)+w with u+(v+w). Write the displacement needed to return from the final point to the start,and show it closes the route. Distinguish displacement from total distance travelled.
items.teacher: u+v=[2;2];total[1;0]. v+w=[−3;3];both groupings give[1;0]. Return[−1;0],sumzero. A route's path length is not its resultant;the optional exact total distance is5+sqrt29+sqrt5 metres,not1m. Do not require that radical calculation before Lesson8. Geometry and component sums must agree.

items.title: Scaling,direction and the zero vector
items.student: Let a=[2;−1]. Draw a,3a,−2a,0a and(1/2)a from a common origin. Compute each column. Describe length and direction relative to a,including what cannot be said about the direction of0a. Show that2(a+b)=2a+2b for b=[−1;3] by components and a sketch. Use squared paper large enough for half-unit marks.
items.teacher: 3a=[6;−3],−2a=[−4;2],0a=[0;0],a/2=[1;−0.5]. Positive factors preserve direction,negative reverse it,magnitude scales by absolute factor. Zero has no unique direction. a+b=[1;2];both doubled expressions[2;4]. Define subtraction as adding the negative vector for later displacements. Halves are components,not a change in the declared grid scale.

items.title: Position depends on the origin;displacement does not
items.student: With O(0,0),P(−2,3),Q(4,−1),write OP,OQ and PQ as columns. Draw the triangle and explain PQ=OQ−OP. Now choose R(1,1) as the reference point:find RP,RQ and RQ−RP. Which position vectors changed and which displacement did not? Mark every chosen origin explicitly.
items.teacher: OP=[−2;3],OQ=[4;−1],PQ=[6;−4]. Relative to R,RP=[−3;2],RQ=[3;−2];difference[6;−4]. Position vectors depend on the reference;the displacement from P to Q is unchanged when the origin is translated. Subtraction adds the opposite vector and is componentwise. Do not confuse a point's new coordinates with physical motion of the point.

items.title: Magnitude is a nonnegative length
items.student: Use a right triangle to derive the magnitude of v=[3;4] grid metres. Find magnitudes of−v,[6;8],[−5;12] and[0;0]. A route goes3m east then4m north:state distance travelled and displacement magnitude. Explain why a negative component cannot make a negative magnitude. Keep exact values where appropriate.
items.teacher: |[p;q]|=sqrt(p²+q²) by Pythagoras. Answers5m,5m,10m,13m,0m. The route distance7m,resultant magnitude5m. Components may be signed;length is nonnegative. This formula requires orthogonal equal-unit axes,not a diagram with arbitrary unequal scales. Zero-vector direction is not defined,not zero degrees.

items.title: Where is halfway along a directed segment?
items.student: For A(−2,1),B(4,5),find AB and the midpoint M in two ways:average endpoint coordinates,and A+(1/2)AB. Check AM=MB. Repeat for C(−3,−1),D(2,4),allowing fractional coordinates. Explain the difference between the midpoint's position vector and half of AB. Here the curriculum's midpoint-of-a-vector wording means the midpoint of its displayed directed segment.
items.teacher: AB=[6;4],M(1,3),AM=MB=[3;2]. CD=[5;5],midpoint(−0.5,1.5),CM=MD=[2.5;2.5]. HalfAB=[3;2] is displacement from A to M;OM=[1;3] is the midpoint position relative to O. They coincide only when A is O. A free vector alone has no fixed midpoint location until a representative startpoint is specified.

items.title: A translation moves every vertex by one vector
items.student: Triangle A(−1,1),B(2,1),C(0,3) is translated by t=[3;−2]. Plot the original and image,find A',B',C',and recover t from each matched pair. Compare AB with A'B'. A proposed image D'(2,1) is claimed to be the image of D(0,0) under the same t;check that claim. No rotation,enlargement or change of axis scale is involved.
items.teacher: A'(2,−1),B'(5,−1),C'(3,1). Every difference is[3;−2];AB=A'B'=[3;0]. D should map to(3,−2),so the proposed point gives a different vector[2;1]. Translation preserves corresponding displacement vectors,lengths and orientation. Check all vertices;one point alone cannot validate a complete polygon image.

items.title: What do route arrows really tell us?
items.student: Paper campus map:East is positive x,North positive y,one coordinate unit=10m. A messenger starts S(0,0),travels to T(3,0),then U(3,4),then V(1,4). Find each displacement,total distance,resultant and its magnitude. Where should a collection point halfway from S to V lie? Explain why a one-way road sign alone cannot specify a displacement magnitude. Design a safe paper route change and justify a vector benefit;do not enter roads or act as traffic.
items.teacher: ST=[3;0],TU=[0;4],UV=[−2;0];physical displacements30m east,40m north,20m west. Distance90m,resultant[1;4]grid units=[10;40]m,magnitude10sqrt17≈41.23m. Midpoint(0.5,2)grid coordinates=(5m,20m)relative to S. Direction-only road arrows lack a scale/magnitude and may encode a traffic instruction rather than a quantitative vector. Any revised pupil route requires teacher checking of its actual coordinates/scale;no unsupported route answer is supplied.

items.title: Audit a reproducible vector model
items.student: Audit four claims: A vectors[2;3]and[−2;−3]are equivalent because their lengths agree; B midpoint of A(2,2),B(6,4)is[2;1]; C translating a triangle means adding the same vector to every vertex; D magnitude of[−3;4]is−5. Repair false statements with diagrams/calculations. In pairs make a small labelled vector-addition or translation chart on reused paper,exchange and check. If approved devices are available,plot a translated triangle in a spreadsheet or teacher-selected vector tool,record the actual tool/inputs/output and check against paper. Paper work alone is not a completed digital action.
items.teacher: A false:opposite directions;B midpoint position(4,3),whereas halfAB=[2;1]is displacement from A;C true;D magnitude5. Every learner supplies one independent correction before sharing. Device task is optional implementation of suggested digital activity;teacher provides approved tool and access,records observed/not-observed action and avoids account/personal-data entry. Confirm actual pupil-created charts rather than assuming group success demonstrates each learner's skill.

items.title: Independent vector audit data
items.student: For the separate final prompts,use equal-unit Cartesian axes with east positive x,north positive y. One unit=1m. Points O(0,0),A(−1,2),B(3,5),C(1,−2),D(5,1). Vectors u=[2;−1],v=[−1;3]. Triangle P(−2,0),Q(0,0),R(−1,2) is translated by t=[3;−1]. Use the supplied blank assessment grid or squared paper and label arrowheads,origins,scale and units. These are fictional paper data only. No teaching cards,worked examples or peer discussion during assessment.
items.teacher: Final1:mass5kg scalar;displacement4m west vector;AB=CD=[4;3]equivalent,BA=[−4;−3]opposite;OB=[3;5]differs fromAB. Final2:u+v=[1;2],−2u=[−4;2],u−v=[3;−4],|u−v|=5m;head-to-tail u→v ends(1,2);component checks required. Final3:M ofAB=(1,3.5),AM=MB=[2;1.5];halfAB differs fromOM. P'(1,−1),Q'(3,−1),R'(2,1),each shift[3;−1],PQ=P'Q'=[2;0]. Final4:one concrete benefit linked to a checked result;road arrow direction alone lacks quantitative magnitude and is not permission to use an unsafe route. Do not release teacher results.
